headline: Chromosome-scale genomes link structure to compartmentalization and nitrogen fixation
label: Chromosome Scale Genome Assemblies
summary: Chromosome-scale nuclear and organellar assemblies now resolve genome architecture in a fungal pathogen, a nitroplast host, and Arctic plant lineages.
synthesis: The common thread is genome architecture resolved at chromosome scale, with organellar genomes included. The Anisogramma anomala preprint reports chromosome-scale nuclear and mitochondrial assemblies and attributes its extreme compartmentalization to a transposable-element-driven two-speed architecture. The Braarudosphaera bigelowii preprint assembles 472.1-Mb nuclear and organellar genomes for a nitroplast-hosting haptophyte and links them to remodeling of nitrogen metabolism. The third preprint addresses Arctic adaptation in distantly related plant lineages, framing shared genomic signatures as possible convergent responses to extreme selection pressure; its summary does not report assembly-level results. What is new is linking resolved genome structure to mechanistic interpretation, here compartment organization and organelle-host metabolism, rather than contig-level description. The items are heterogeneous, so this coupling is not shared by the Arctic study.
